title: How to surpass no-go limits in Gaussian quantum error correction and entangled Gaussian state distillation

predicted_errors.error_location: Discussion/Application section, numeric threshold statement: "For typical noise levels satisfying σ² < π³/(4√(2e)) ≈ 1.012, it is clear that this concatenation always yields benefits for r > 0."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Computing the stated expression: π³ ≈ 31.006, √(2e) ≈ 2.3316, so 4√(2e) ≈ 9.3265. Then π³/(4√(2e)) ≈ 31.006/9.3265 ≈ 3.325, not 1.012 as claimed. The numerical value given in the text does not match the formula it is supposed to evaluate, a roughly 3.3x discrepancy that is not attributable to rounding.

predicted_errors.error_location: Text following Eq. (17): "it is clear that this concatenation always yields benefits for r > 0"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (17) states the benefit condition as 4/ln(π^1.5/(2σ^4)) + 1 < e^{4r}. As r→0+, the right-hand side e^{4r}→1, while the left-hand side equals 4/L+1 > 1 for any finite positive L = ln(π^1.5/(2σ^4)). Hence the inequality fails for sufficiently small r>0, contradicting the claim that benefits hold for 'all r>0'; the condition can only hold above some strictly positive threshold r*, not for every r>0.
